grammarTopics.title: Past of Be: Was, Were, There Was/Were
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Fungsi was/were
**Was** dan **were** adalah bentuk lampau dari *am/is/are*. Dipakai untuk tempat, keadaan, perasaan, dan deskripsi di masa lalu: *I **was** at home yesterday. The film **was** boring.*

| Subjek | Positif | Negatif | Pertanyaan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I / he / she / it | was | wasn't | Was he...? |
| you / we / they | were | weren't | Were you...? |

### There was / there were
Untuk menyatakan *ada* di masa lalu: **there was** + benda tunggal/tak terhitung, **there were** + benda jamak. *There was a storm. There were fifty guests.*

### Penting
Was/were **tidak** memakai *did*: ✗ *Did you were tired?* ✓ *Were you tired?* Jawaban singkat: *Yes, I was. / No, they weren't.*

formulas.label: There was/were
formulas.pattern: There was + singular/uncountable; There were + plural

positive: I was at the dentist yesterday.
My grandparents were teachers.
There was a big crowd at the stadium.
negative: The shops weren't open on Sunday.
She wasn't happy with the hotel.
There weren't any taxis at the station.
interrogative: Where were you last night?
Was the exam difficult?
Were there any problems?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja untuk masa lampau (*Saya capek kemarin*). Bahasa Inggris wajib mengubah *am/is* menjadi **was** dan *are* menjadi **were**: *I **was** tired yesterday.*

mistakes.why: Pertanyaan dengan was/were tidak memakai did.

mistakes.wrong: There was two cats in the garden.
mistakes.right: There were two cats in the garden.

exercises.prompt: Write was, were, wasn't or weren't.
exercises.text: Last Sunday the beach ___ very crowded, but the water ___ clean. My friends ___ there because they were sick.
exercises.explanation: The beach → was. Air tidak bersih (but) → wasn't. Teman-teman tidak ada di sana karena sakit → weren't.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct option: ___ a lot of people at the night market yesterday?
exercises.explanation: People jamak → Were there...? Pertanyaan tidak memakai did.

exercises.prompt: Correct the question.
exercises.explanation: Untuk to be, pertanyaannya cukup dengan menukar posisi: Was the concert good?

grammarTopics.title: Past Simple: Regular, Irregular, Negatives and Questions
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Fungsi past simple
Past simple dipakai untuk kegiatan yang **sudah selesai** di masa lalu, biasanya dengan waktu yang jelas: *yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago*.

### Bentuk positif
- Beraturan: **verb + -ed** (*worked, studied, stopped, lived*).
- Tidak beraturan: dihafal (*went, had, saw, bought, took, made*).
- Bentuknya sama untuk semua subjek.

### Negatif dan pertanyaan
Gunakan **did** + bentuk dasar:

| Bentuk | Pola | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Negatif | didn't + base verb | *She didn't go.* |
| Yes/No | Did + subject + base verb? | *Did you see it?* |
| Wh- | Wh- + did + subject + base verb? | *Where did they stay?* |

Pertanyaan subjek tidak memakai did: *Who called you? What happened?*

### Pelafalan -ed
/t/ setelah bunyi tak bersuara (*worked*), /d/ setelah bunyi bersuara (*played*), /ɪd/ setelah t/d (*wanted*).

positive: We visited the museum last Saturday.
She bought a new bag and went home.
I studied until midnight.
negative: I didn't sleep well.
They didn't take a taxi.
He didn't answer my message.
interrogative: Did you enjoy the trip?
What did you eat for lunch?
Who told you the news?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *tidak* tanpa mengubah kata kerja (*Dia tidak pergi*). Bahasa Inggris butuh **didn't** dan kata kerja kembali ke bentuk dasar: *She didn't go* (bukan *didn't went*).

mistakes.why: Pertanyaan wh- butuh did + base verb.
Buy adalah kata kerja tidak beraturan.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past simple of the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: Yesterday I ___ (take) the bus to work, but I ___ (not / bring) my umbrella, so I ___ (get) wet.
exercises.explanation: take → took; negatif → didn't bring (bentuk dasar); get → got.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
exercises.explanation: How long + did + you + stay (bentuk dasar) + tempat.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake.
exercises.explanation: Setelah did, kata kerja kembali ke bentuk dasar: find.

grammarTopics.title: Comparatives, Superlatives and As ... As
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Membandingkan
| Jenis adjective | Comparative | Superlative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pendek (cheap) | cheaper than | the cheapest |
| berakhiran -e (nice) | nicer than | the nicest |
| vokal + konsonan (big) | bigger than | the biggest |
| berakhiran -y (easy) | easier than | the easiest |
| panjang (expensive) | more expensive than | the most expensive |
| good / bad / far | better / worse / further | the best / the worst / the furthest |

### As ... as
**as + adjective + as** = sama (*as tall as*). **not as + adjective + as** = kurang (*not as cheap as*). Adjective tetap bentuk dasar.

### Penting
Jangan gabungkan *more* dan *-er* (✗ *more bigger*). Pakai **than** untuk comparative, dan **the** untuk superlative.

formulas.label: Comparative
formulas.pattern: A + be + adjective-er / more + adjective + than + B

formulas.label: Superlative
formulas.pattern: the + adjective-est / the most + adjective (+ in/of ...)

formulas.label: Sama
formulas.pattern: A + be + as + adjective + as + B

formulas.label: Kurang
formulas.pattern: A + be + not as + adjective + as + B

positive: The train is faster than the bus.
This is the most comfortable hotel in town.
My bag is as heavy as yours.
negative: The village isn't as noisy as the city.
This phone isn't better than my old one.
It wasn't the worst film of the year.
interrogative: Which is cheaper, the red one or the blue one?
Who is the tallest person in your family?
Is Bandung as hot as Jakarta?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *lebih ... daripada*, *paling*, dan *se-* (*setinggi*). Bahasa Inggris memilih **-er/more**, **-est/most** berdasarkan panjang adjective, dan **as ... as** untuk *se-*.

mistakes.wrong: She is more taller than me.
My room is as big than yours.
mistakes.right: My room is as big as yours.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct form of the adjectives in brackets.
exercises.text: Riverton is ___ (big) than Sunny Bay, but Sunny Bay has ___ (good) beaches in the region.
exercises.explanation: Membandingkan dua kota → bigger than. Di antara semua pantai di wilayah → the best.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it has the same meaning.
exercises.sentence: The bus is slower than the train.
exercises.cue: Begin with: The bus isn't as ...
answers: The bus isn't as fast as the train.
The bus is not as fast as the train.
exercises.explanation: Bus lebih lambat = bus tidak secepat kereta: isn't as fast as.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct option: It was ___ day of my holiday. It rained all day and I lost my wallet.
exercises.explanation: Superlative dari bad adalah the worst.

grammarTopics.title: Future Forms: Going To, Present Continuous, Will
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Tiga cara membicarakan masa depan
| Bentuk | Fungsi | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **be going to** + verb | rencana/niat yang sudah diputuskan | *I'm going to learn Japanese.* |
| **be going to** + verb | prediksi dengan bukti sekarang | *Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.* |
| **present continuous** | acara yang sudah diatur (waktu/tempat/orang) | *I'm meeting Sara at six tomorrow.* |
| **will** + verb | keputusan spontan, tawaran | *I'll help you.* |
| **will** + verb | janji | *I won't forget, I promise.* |
| **will** + verb | prediksi berdasarkan pendapat | *I think it will be sunny.* |

### Tips memilih
- Sudah diputuskan sebelumnya? → **going to**
- Sudah ada jadwal/janji dengan orang lain? → **present continuous**
- Diputuskan saat berbicara, menawarkan, berjanji? → **will**

formulas.label: Going to
formulas.pattern: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb

positive: We're going to paint the house next month.
I'm flying to Medan on Friday.
I'll carry that bag for you.
negative: She isn't going to apply for the job.
We aren't having a party this year.
I won't tell anyone.
interrogative: What are you going to do after the exam?
Are you doing anything on Saturday?
Will you be home tonight?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *akan* untuk semua bentuk masa depan. Bahasa Inggris membedakan rencana (**going to**), jadwal (**present continuous**), dan keputusan/janji/pendapat (**will**).

mistakes.wrong: I going to visit my aunt.
mistakes.right: I'm going to visit my aunt.

mistakes.wrong: The phone is ringing. I answer it.
mistakes.right: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best future form.
exercises.text: A: Do you have plans for Saturday? B: Yes, ___ my cousin at the airport at ten. She's arriving from Bali. A: That bag looks heavy. B: Oh, thanks! A: Don't worry, ___ it for you.
exercises.explanation: Jadwal yang sudah diatur (jam 10 di bandara) → present continuous. Tawaran spontan → I'll carry.

exercises.prompt: Choose the best option: Look at that boy on the wall! He ___ fall.
exercises.explanation: Prediksi dengan bukti yang terlihat sekarang → is going to.

exercises.prompt: Translate into English. (a plan you made last month)
exercises.source: Kami akan pindah ke Surabaya tahun depan.
answers: We're going to move to Surabaya next year.
We are going to move to Surabaya next year.
Next year we're going to move to Surabaya.
We're moving to Surabaya next year.
We are moving to Surabaya next year.
exercises.explanation: Rencana yang sudah diputuskan → be going to (present continuous juga diterima).

grammarTopics.title: Should, Have To, Must
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Empat makna penting
| Bentuk | Arti | Contoh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **should / shouldn't** | saran (ide baik/buruk) | *You should see a doctor.* |
| **have to / has to** | wajib (karena aturan/keadaan) | *Nurses have to work at night.* |
| **must** | wajib (aturan kuat) | *You must wear a seatbelt.* |
| **mustn't** | **dilarang** | *You mustn't smoke here.* |
| **don't have to** | **tidak perlu** | *You don't have to pay. It's free.* |

### Bentuk
- *should* dan *must* tidak berubah untuk he/she dan tidak memakai *to*: *She should rest.*
- *have to* berubah seperti kata kerja biasa: *he **has to**, he **doesn't have to**, **Do** you have to...?*
- Masa lalu: **had to** (tidak ada *musted*).

### Jangan tertukar
**mustn't** = tidak boleh; **don't have to** = tidak perlu.

formulas.label: Kewajiban
formulas.pattern: Subject + have to/has to/must + base verb

formulas.label: Tidak perlu
formulas.pattern: Subject + don't/doesn't have to + base verb

positive: You should drink more water.
She has to wear a uniform.
Visitors must sign in at reception.
negative: You shouldn't stay up late.
We don't have to work on Sunday.
You mustn't park here.
interrogative: Should I take this medicine?
Do you have to get up early?
What should we do?

grammarTopics.comparison: Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *tidak harus* bisa berarti *tidak perlu* atau *tidak boleh*. Dalam bahasa Inggris maknanya dipisah: **don't have to** (tidak perlu) dan **mustn't** (tidak boleh).

mistakes.right: It's free. You don't have to pay.

exercises.prompt: Drag the correct words into the gaps.
exercises.text: At our school, students ___ wear a uniform from Monday to Thursday, but on Friday they ___ wear it. They ___ use their phones in class. That's a strict rule.
exercises.explanation: Wajib → have to; tidak wajib → don't have to; dilarang (aturan ketat) → mustn't.

exercises.prompt: Your friend has a bad cough. What is the best advice?
options: You should drink some warm water with honey.
You don't have to see a doctor ever.
exercises.explanation: Saran yang masuk akal dan benar secara tata bahasa: You should + base verb.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the correct form of have to.
exercises.text: Yesterday my brother ___ work until ten p.m. ___ he work late today too?
exercises.explanation: Masa lalu → had to. Pertanyaan untuk he → Does he have to...?

grammarTopics.title: Past Continuous and Past Simple
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Past continuous
**was/were + verb-ing** untuk kegiatan yang **sedang berlangsung** pada waktu tertentu di masa lalu, atau sebagai latar cerita: *At 8 p.m. I **was cooking**. The sun **was shining**.*

### Bersama past simple
Kegiatan panjang (past continuous) disela kejadian singkat (past simple):
- *I **was walking** home **when** it **started** to rain.*
- ***While** we **were waiting**, the bus **arrived**.*

| Kata | Biasanya diikuti |
| --- | --- |
| when | past simple (kejadian singkat) |
| while | past continuous (kegiatan panjang) |

### Kata kerja keadaan
*know, like, want, need* biasanya tidak memakai -ing: ✗ *I was knowing*.

positive: At nine o'clock I was having breakfast.
They were playing football when it started to rain.
While she was reading, the lights went out.
negative: I wasn't sleeping when you called.
We weren't watching TV at that time.
He wasn't wearing a helmet.
interrogative: What were you doing at 10 p.m.?
Was it raining when you left?
Were they waiting long?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *sedang* (*Saya sedang makan ketika dia datang*). Bahasa Inggris memakai **was/were + -ing** untuk *sedang* dan **past simple** untuk kejadian yang menyela.

mistakes.wrong: I was cook when she arrived.
mistakes.right: I was cooking when she arrived.

mistakes.wrong: While I walked home, I was seeing an accident.
mistakes.right: While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
mistakes.why: Kegiatan panjang → past continuous; kejadian singkat → past simple.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the past simple or past continuous of the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: While Dani ___ (cook) dinner, he ___ (cut) his finger.
exercises.explanation: While + kegiatan panjang → was cooking. Kejadian singkat → cut (cut – cut – cut).

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
acceptedAnswers: When we saw a beautiful rainbow, we were driving along the coast.
exercises.explanation: Kegiatan panjang (were driving) + when + kejadian singkat (saw).

exercises.prompt: Choose the best reply.

dialogue.speaker: Rina
dialogue.text: I called you at nine last night, but you didn't answer.

options: Sorry, I was having a shower.
Sorry, I was have a shower.
exercises.explanation: Kegiatan yang sedang berlangsung jam sembilan tadi malam → past continuous: I was having a shower.

grammarTopics.title: Present Perfect for Experiences
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Fungsi
Present perfect (**have/has + past participle**) dipakai untuk **pengalaman hidup** sampai sekarang, ketika waktunya tidak disebutkan: *I've visited Japan. Have you ever ridden a horse?*

### Ever, never, been, gone
- **ever** dalam pertanyaan: *Have you **ever** tried durian?*
- **never** = tidak pernah: *I've **never** flown.*
- **been to** = pernah pergi dan sudah kembali; **gone to** = sudah pergi dan belum kembali.

### Present perfect vs past simple
| Present perfect | Past simple |
| --- | --- |
| waktu tidak disebutkan | waktu spesifik |
| *I've been to Bali.* | *I went there in 2021.* |

Untuk detail (when, where, who with), beralihlah ke past simple.

formulas.label: Negatif
formulas.pattern: Subject + haven't/hasn't + past participle / have never + past participle

positive: I've eaten sushi many times.
She has been to Korea twice.
They've won three competitions.
negative: I've never seen snow.
He hasn't driven a car.
We haven't tried that restaurant.
interrogative: Have you ever been to Lombok?
Has she ever met a famous person?
How many times have you flown?

grammarTopics.comparison: Present perfect sering diterjemahkan *pernah* atau *sudah pernah*. *Belum pernah* = **have never** + participle.

mistakes.wrong: I have visited Bali last year.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the present perfect of the verbs in brackets.
exercises.text: My father ___ (drive) a lot of different cars, but he ___ (never / ride) a motorbike.
exercises.explanation: drive → driven, ride → ridden. My father = he → has.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct forms.
exercises.text: A: ___ you ever been to a music festival? B: Yes. I ___ to one in Jakarta last August.
exercises.explanation: Pengalaman → Have you ever been...? Detail dengan last August → past simple went.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct option: Dad isn't home. He's ___ to the mosque.
exercises.explanation: Ayah belum kembali → has gone.

grammarTopics.title: Quantifiers and Adverbs of Manner
grammarTopics.explanation:
### Quantifiers
| Arti | Countable (jamak) | Uncountable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| banyak | many / a lot of | much / a lot of |
| sedikit (ada) | a few | a little |
| berapa? | How many...? | How much...? |

*Much* dan *many* paling umum dalam **negatif dan pertanyaan**; dalam kalimat positif pakai **a lot of**. Ingat: *information, advice, work, money, luggage* = uncountable.

### Adverbs of manner
Menjelaskan **bagaimana** sesuatu dilakukan: adjective + **-ly** (*quickly, carefully, easily*). Tidak beraturan: **good → well**, **fast → fast**, **hard → hard**, **late → late**. Letakkan setelah kata kerja atau objek: *She speaks English **well**.*

formulas.label: Countable
formulas.pattern: many / a few / a lot of + plural noun

formulas.label: Uncountable
formulas.pattern: much / a little / a lot of + uncountable noun

formulas.label: Adverb
formulas.pattern: verb (+ object) + adjective-ly / well / fast / hard

positive: We have a lot of customers today.
There's a little milk left.
She works hard and speaks politely.
negative: I don't have much time.
There aren't many buses after ten.
He doesn't drive carefully.
interrogative: How many people work here?
How much luggage do you have?
Can you speak more slowly?

grammarTopics.comparison: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *banyak* dan *sedikit* untuk semua benda. Bahasa Inggris membedakan countable (**many, a few**) dan uncountable (**much, a little**). *Dengan cepat* = **quickly**, *dengan baik* = **well**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct quantifiers.
exercises.text: How ___ luggage do you have? — Not ___. Just one small bag and ___ souvenirs.
exercises.explanation: Luggage uncountable → How much; Not much. Souvenirs countable → a few.

exercises.prompt: Which sentences are correct? Choose all correct answers.
options: Please speak quietly in the library.
The children played happily in the garden.
exercises.explanation: Seharusnya answered easily (adverb) dan worked hard (hardly = hampir tidak).

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence.
exercises.sentence: There aren't much tables free in the café.
answers: There aren't many tables free in the café.
There are not many tables free in the café.
There aren't many free tables in the café.
exercises.explanation: Tables countable (jamak) → many.

reading.title: A Weekend in the Hills
reading.body:
Hi Nadia,

How are you? I'm sorry I didn't reply to your message last week. I was away for the weekend with my sister and two of her friends.

We went to a small village in the hills about three hours from the city. We left early on Saturday morning and arrived at about ten. The village was really quiet and the air was cool and fresh. There weren't any big hotels, so we stayed in a family guesthouse. The owner, Pak Wayan, was very friendly. On the first evening he cooked a delicious dinner for us with vegetables from his own garden.

On Sunday we got up at five and walked up the hill to watch the sunrise. It was hard work and I was tired, but the view from the top was amazing. I took about a hundred photos! After breakfast we visited a tea plantation and bought some tea for our parents.

The only problem was the road home. It rained heavily on Sunday afternoon, and the traffic was terrible. We didn't get home until eleven at night.

Are you free next Saturday? I can show you the photos.

Love,
Meli

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Meli's email?
options: To tell Nadia about her weekend trip
To book a room at a guesthouse
To invite Nadia to a tea plantation
questions.explanation: Sebagian besar email menceritakan perjalanan akhir pekan Meli ke desa di perbukitan (main idea).

questions.prompt: Why did they stay in a guesthouse?
options: There weren't any big hotels in the village.
The guesthouse was near the tea plantation.
questions.explanation: Teks: There weren't any big hotels, so we stayed in a family guesthouse.

questions.prompt: How long was the journey home on Sunday?
options: Longer than the journey to the village
Shorter than the journey to the village
About three hours, the same as usual
The text doesn't say they went home
questions.explanation: Perjalanan berangkat sekitar tiga jam, tetapi saat pulang hujan lebat dan macet sehingga mereka baru tiba jam 11 malam. Jadi perjalanan pulang lebih lama (inferensi).

questions.prompt: In the text, 'the view from the top was amazing'. What does 'amazing' mean?
questions.explanation: Meli mengambil sekitar seratus foto, jadi pemandangannya sangat indah — amazing = luar biasa.

questions.prompt: What did they buy at the tea plantation?
questions.explanation: Teks: we visited a tea plantation and bought some tea for our parents.

reading.title: The Wrong Suitcase
reading.body:
Last December, Arman was flying home from a work trip. It was a long day. His first flight was delayed, so he nearly missed his connection. When he finally landed in Makassar, it was almost midnight and he was very tired.

While he was waiting at the baggage belt, he was thinking about his bed. A black suitcase came round, and he took it quickly. Then he caught a taxi and went home.

At home, Arman opened the suitcase. He was looking for his toothbrush, but he found a pink dress, a pair of high-heeled shoes and a book in Japanese! It wasn't his suitcase. He looked at the label. The name on it was Yuki Tanaka, and there was a phone number.

Arman called the number immediately. A woman answered. She was still at the airport, and she was very worried because her suitcase was missing. Arman explained the situation and apologised. The next morning, he took the suitcase back to the airport, and Yuki gave him his own black suitcase. It looked exactly the same as hers!

Now Arman always ties a bright orange ribbon to his luggage.

questions.prompt: What is the story mainly about?
options: A man who took someone else's suitcase by mistake
A woman who lost her passport
A man who missed his flight
A taxi driver at the airport
questions.explanation: Inti cerita: Arman salah mengambil koper milik orang lain lalu mengembalikannya.

questions.prompt: What was Arman doing when he found the dress?
questions.explanation: Teks: He was looking for his toothbrush, but he found a pink dress...

questions.prompt: Why does Arman now tie an orange ribbon to his luggage?
options: So he can recognise his suitcase easily
Because orange is Yuki's favourite colour
Because the airport asked him to
So the suitcase looks more expensive
questions.explanation: Kedua koper terlihat sama persis. Pita oranye membantunya mengenali kopernya sendiri (inferensi).

questions.prompt: 'Arman called the number immediately.' What does 'immediately' mean?
questions.explanation: Immediately = segera, tanpa menunggu.

reading.title: Riverton or Sunny Bay?
reading.body:
Are you thinking of moving to a new city? Riverton and Sunny Bay are two popular choices, but they are very different.

Riverton is the biggest city in the region, with more than two million people. It's more modern than Sunny Bay, and there are a lot of shopping malls, offices and international restaurants. It's also the best place to find a job, especially in technology and finance. However, life in Riverton is expensive. Rents are much higher than in Sunny Bay, and the traffic is terrible in the morning and evening. The air is also more polluted.

Sunny Bay is a smaller town on the coast. It isn't as exciting as Riverton, and there aren't many big companies there. But it's cleaner, safer and much more peaceful. Most people live near the beach, and a lot of them go to work by bicycle. The cost of living is lower, so a salary goes further. The town is also famous for its seafood, which is cheaper and fresher than in Riverton.

So which city is better? It depends on you. If you want a busy career, Riverton is probably the right choice. If you prefer a quiet life, Sunny Bay is hard to beat.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the article?
options: Riverton and Sunny Bay are good for different kinds of people.
Sunny Bay is better than Riverton in every way.
Riverton is too expensive for everyone.
Everybody in Sunny Bay works in technology.
questions.explanation: Artikel membandingkan kedua kota dan menyimpulkan bahwa pilihannya tergantung pada orangnya.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about Sunny Bay is true?
options: It has more big companies than Riverton.
It is more modern than Riverton.
Rents are higher than in Riverton.
questions.explanation: Teks: it's cleaner, safer and much more peaceful.

questions.prompt: Who would probably prefer Riverton?
options: A young engineer who wants a job at a big technology company
A retired couple who want a quiet life by the sea
A family who want cheap fresh seafood
Someone who likes cycling to work on quiet roads
questions.explanation: Riverton adalah tempat terbaik untuk mencari kerja, terutama di bidang teknologi (inferensi dari teks).

questions.prompt: 'If you prefer a quiet life, Sunny Bay is hard to beat.' What does 'hard to beat' mean here?
options: very difficult to find a better choice
questions.explanation: Hard to beat = sulit dikalahkan, artinya pilihan yang sangat bagus.

reading.title: Company Starts Healthy Workplace Plan
reading.body:
Staff at Brightway Software in Green Hill are going to start a new healthy workplace programme next month. The company's manager, Mrs. Siregar, decided to start the programme because a lot of employees were feeling tired and stressed.

"Many of our staff sit at their computers for nine or ten hours a day," she said. "They don't get enough exercise, and they often eat junk food at their desks. We want to change that."

Under the new plan, there will be some new rules. Employees must take a fifteen-minute break every two hours, and they mustn't eat lunch at their desks. The canteen is going to serve healthier food, with more fruit and vegetables and fewer fried snacks. Staff don't have to join the free yoga classes on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, but the company hopes that many of them will try.

Not everyone is happy. "I have a lot of work, and I don't have much time for breaks," said one programmer. But most staff like the idea. "I think it's great," said Dodi, a designer. "Last year I had terrible backaches. My doctor said I should move more. Now I'll have time to do that at work."

questions.prompt: What is the news story about?
options: A company's new plan to make its staff healthier
A new yoga school in Green Hill
A programmer who lost his job
A canteen that closed last month
questions.explanation: Berita ini tentang program tempat kerja sehat di Brightway Software.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a rule? Staff ___
options: have to go to yoga classes.
must take a break every two hours.
mustn't eat lunch at their desks.
can eat healthier food in the canteen.
questions.explanation: Teks: Staff don't have to join the free yoga classes — kelas yoga tidak wajib.

questions.prompt: Why is the programmer not happy about the plan?
options: He thinks the breaks will make it harder to finish his work.
He thinks the canteen food is too expensive.
questions.explanation: Dia berkata punya banyak pekerjaan dan tidak punya banyak waktu untuk istirahat — jadi dia khawatir pekerjaannya tidak selesai (inferensi).

questions.prompt: 'They often eat junk food at their desks.' What is 'junk food'?
options: food that is quick to eat but not healthy
food that you cook at home
questions.explanation: Junk food = makanan cepat saji/tidak sehat. Kontrasnya: the canteen is going to serve healthier food.

reading.title: The Job Interview
reading.body:
Mr. Hakim: Good morning, Ms. Putri. Please sit down. Would you like some water?
Putri: Yes, please. Thank you.
Mr. Hakim: So, why would you like to work at the Grand Palm Hotel?
Putri: I've always enjoyed working with people, and your hotel has a very good name. I'd like to learn more about hotel management.
Mr. Hakim: Have you ever worked in a hotel before?
Putri: Yes, I have. I worked as a receptionist at a small guesthouse in Lombok for two years. I left last March because I moved to Surabaya with my family.
Mr. Hakim: What did you do there?
Putri: I checked guests in and out, answered the phone and dealt with problems. Sometimes I had to work the night shift.
Mr. Hakim: How many languages do you speak?
Putri: I speak Indonesian and English, and a little Japanese. I studied it for a year at university.
Mr. Hakim: Very good. The job is full-time, and you'll have to work some weekends. Is that a problem?
Putri: No, not at all. I don't mind working at weekends.
Mr. Hakim: Excellent. We'll call you next week.

questions.prompt: What is happening in the dialogue?
options: Putri is having an interview for a hotel job.
Putri is booking a room at the Grand Palm Hotel.
Mr. Hakim is asking Putri for directions.
Putri is complaining about her room.
questions.explanation: Mr. Hakim menanyakan pengalaman dan kemampuan Putri untuk pekerjaan di hotel — ini wawancara kerja.

questions.prompt: Why did Putri leave her job in Lombok?
options: She moved to Surabaya with her family.
She didn't like the night shifts.
questions.explanation: Putri: I left last March because I moved to Surabaya with my family.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Hakim probably think of Putri?
options: He has a good opinion of her.
He thinks she doesn't have enough experience.
He thinks her English is very bad.
questions.explanation: Dia berkata Very good dan Excellent, jadi kesannya positif (inferensi).

questions.prompt: 'I don't mind working at weekends.' What does Putri mean?
options: Working at weekends is OK for her.
She doesn't want to work at weekends.
She always works at weekends now.
questions.explanation: I don't mind = saya tidak keberatan, artinya bekerja di akhir pekan tidak masalah baginya.

script.speaker: Ayu

script.speaker: Ayu

Because Reza is helping her dad

speaking.title: Tell Me About Your Weekend
speaking.prompt: A colleague asks: 'How was your weekend?' Talk for 45–60 seconds. Say where you went, who you were with, what you did, and how you felt. Use the past simple and was/were.
speaking.sampleAnswer: It was really nice, thanks! On Saturday morning I cleaned my flat and did some shopping. In the afternoon I met my cousin and we went to a new café near the river. The coffee was great, but it was quite expensive. On Sunday I visited my grandparents. My grandmother cooked soto ayam, and we ate in the garden. We didn't do anything special, but I was very relaxed.
tips: Mulai dengan kesan umum: It was great / relaxing / busy.
Urutkan dengan On Saturday morning, In the afternoon, On Sunday.
Pastikan semua kata kerja dalam bentuk lampau (went, met, ate).

speaking.title: Booking a Hotel Room
speaking.prompt: You are calling a hotel. Book a room for you and your partner for three nights next weekend. Ask about the price, breakfast, and check-out time.
targetPhrases: Do you have any rooms available
Can I book a double room
How much is it per night
speaking.sampleAnswer: Good morning. Do you have any rooms available from Friday to Monday? ... Great. Can I book a double room for three nights, please? ... How much is it per night? ... Is breakfast included? ... And what time is check-out? ... OK, my name is Dewi Kartika, D-E-W-I. Thank you very much!
tips: Gunakan Can I... atau Could I... agar sopan.
Ulangi informasi penting untuk memastikan: Three nights, from Friday?
Eja namamu dengan jelas.

speaking.title: Giving Health Advice
speaking.prompt: Your friend says: 'I have a headache every afternoon at work and I often feel tired.' Ask one or two questions about their habits, then give advice using should, shouldn't and have to.
targetPhrases: How many hours do you sleep
speaking.sampleAnswer: Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that. How many hours do you sleep at night? And do you drink enough water at work? I think you should drink more water and take short breaks. You shouldn't look at your screen for hours without a break. You should also go to bed earlier. And if the headaches don't stop, you have to see a doctor.
tips: Tunjukkan simpati dulu: I'm sorry to hear that.
Tanyakan kebiasaan sebelum memberi saran.
Gunakan I think you should... agar terdengar ramah.

speaking.title: Which One Should I Buy?
speaking.prompt: Compare two things you know well (for example, two phones, two motorbikes, or two cafés). Talk about price, quality, and size, and say which one you prefer and why.
speaking.sampleAnswer: I want to compare two phones, the Nova A5 and the Orbit Pro. The Nova is cheaper than the Orbit, and it's lighter. But the Orbit's camera is much better, and its battery lasts longer. The Nova isn't as fast as the Orbit, but it's fine for messages and social media. In my opinion, the Nova is the best choice for students, because it's good value.
tips: Gunakan setidaknya satu comparative, satu superlative, dan satu not as ... as.
Beri pendapat dengan In my opinion dan alasan dengan because.

speaking.title: Have You Ever...?
speaking.prompt: Talk about three interesting experiences in your life. For each one, say what you have done (present perfect) and then give details: when, where and how it was (past simple).
speaking.sampleAnswer: I've been to Lombok three times. The last time, I went there with my friends in 2023 and we climbed a small volcano. It was hard but amazing. I've also tried a lot of strange food. Once I ate fried crickets at a night market, and they were crunchy! But I've never flown abroad. I'd like to visit Japan one day.
tips: Mulai dengan present perfect untuk pengalaman umum.
Beralihlah ke past simple saat menyebut waktu (in 2023, last year).
Ingat: been = pernah pergi dan sudah kembali.

speaking.title: Pronunciation: -ed Endings
speaking.prompt: Read these sentences aloud. Pay attention to the -ed endings: /t/, /d/ or /ɪd/. 'I walked to the station and waited for the train. It arrived late, so I called my boss. She laughed and said I needed a new watch!'
speaking.sampleAnswer: I walked /wɔːkt/ to the station and waited /ˈweɪtɪd/ for the train. It arrived /əˈraɪvd/ late, so I called /kɔːld/ my boss. She laughed /lɑːft/ and said I needed /ˈniːdɪd/ a new watch!
tips: Hanya waited dan needed yang menambah suku kata (/ɪd/).
Walked dan laughed diakhiri bunyi /t/ yang pendek, bukan 'ed'.
Rekam suaramu dan bandingkan dengan contoh.

speaking.title: Inviting a Friend
speaking.prompt: Invite a friend to a celebration (a birthday dinner, a graduation party or a concert). Say what it is, when and where. Then imagine your friend can't come on that day, and suggest another plan.
speaking.sampleAnswer: Hi Tono! Are you free on Friday evening? We're having a small dinner for Sari's birthday at the Green Valley Café at seven. Would you like to come? ... Oh, you're working late? That's a pity. How about Saturday, then? Let's have lunch together and bring her a cake. I'll book a table.
tips: Gunakan present continuous untuk acara yang sudah diatur: We're having...
Tawarkan alternatif dengan How about...? atau Let's...
Akhiri dengan janji/keputusan: I'll book a table.

writing.title: A Holiday to Remember
writing.instructions: Tulis cerita tentang liburan atau perjalanan yang kamu ingat. Ceritakan ke mana kamu pergi, dengan siapa, apa yang terjadi (termasuk satu masalah atau kejutan), dan bagaimana perasaanmu. Gunakan past simple, past continuous (when/while), dan sequencers (First, Then, After that, Finally).
writing.modelAnswer: Last year I went to Yogyakarta with my two best friends. First, we visited the old palace, and then we walked along the main street and bought some batik. On the second day we went to a beach in the south. While we were swimming, a big wave took my sunglasses! I was sad, but my friends laughed a lot. After that, we had grilled fish at a small restaurant near the beach. It was the best fish I've ever eaten. Finally, we took the night train home. We were tired, but it was an unforgettable trip.

writing.title: An Invitation Email
writing.instructions: Tulis email informal kepada seorang teman untuk mengundangnya ke sebuah acara (ulang tahun, kelulusan, atau syukuran rumah baru). Sebutkan acara, hari, jam, tempat, apa yang perlu dibawa, dan minta temanmu membalas. Gunakan Hi + nama dan penutup informal.
writing.modelAnswer:
Hi Lina,

How are you? I hope work isn't too busy! I've got some good news: we're moving into our new flat next week. We're having a small housewarming party on Saturday 14th at 7 p.m. The address is 23 Jalan Melati, flat 5B. Would you like to come? You don't have to bring anything, but if you want, you can bring some snacks. Please let me know by Thursday.

See you soon,
Sekar

writing.title: Comparing Two Places
writing.instructions: Tulis paragraf yang membandingkan dua tempat yang kamu kenal (dua kota, dua kafe, atau dua sekolah). Gunakan comparative, superlative, dan as ... as / not as ... as. Akhiri dengan pendapatmu dan alasannya.
writing.modelAnswer: My hometown, Salatiga, is much smaller than Semarang. Semarang is busier and more modern, and there are a lot of shopping malls. However, it's hotter and more crowded, and the traffic is terrible. Salatiga isn't as exciting as Semarang, but it's cooler and more peaceful because it's in the hills. The food is also cheaper. In my opinion, Salatiga is the best place for families, because it's safer and quieter. But for young people who want a career, Semarang is probably better.

writing.title: Booking a Hotel by Email
writing.instructions: Tulis email singkat dan sopan kepada sebuah hotel untuk memesan kamar. Sebutkan jenis kamar, tanggal datang dan pergi, jumlah orang, dan tanyakan dua hal (misalnya sarapan dan parkir). Gunakan Dear Sir or Madam dan Best regards.
writing.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I would like to book a double room for two adults from 12 to 15 June (three nights). We are arriving by car at about 4 p.m. on 12 June.

Could you tell me the price per night? Is breakfast included? I would also like to know if there is free parking at the hotel.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to your reply.

Best regards,
Andi Wijaya

writing.title: Correct the Message
writing.instructions: Pesan berikut memiliki 6 kesalahan tata bahasa. Tulis ulang pesan dengan benar: "Hi Dimas! Last weekend I go to Bandung with my family. We was very tired because the traffic was terrible. On Sunday we visit a tea plantation. It was more bigger than I thought. Did you went to the concert? I'm going call you tomorrow!"
writing.modelAnswer: Hi Dimas! Last weekend I went to Bandung with my family. We were very tired because the traffic was terrible. On Sunday we visited a tea plantation. It was bigger than I thought. Did you go to the concert? I'm going to call you tomorrow!

writing.title: My Dream Job
writing.instructions: Tulis tentang pekerjaan impianmu. Jelaskan pekerjaan apa, di mana, apa yang dilakukan orang dengan pekerjaan itu, mengapa kamu menyukainya, dan apa yang perlu kamu lakukan untuk mendapatkannya. Gunakan want to / would like to / need to, adverbs of manner, dan should/have to.
writing.modelAnswer: My dream job is to be a tour guide in Bali. Tour guides show visitors interesting places and explain the history and culture of the island. I'd like to do this job because I enjoy meeting people from different countries and I love my culture. A good guide has to speak clearly and patiently, and should know a lot about local food and traditions. To get this job, I need to improve my English and learn a little Japanese. I also want to take a course in tourism next year.

vocabulary.definition: not afraid to do dangerous or difficult things

examples.en: You were very brave to swim with sharks!
examples.id: Kamu sangat berani berenang bersama hiu!

vocabulary.definition: so special that you will always remember it

examples.en: Watching the sunrise from the volcano was unforgettable.
examples.id: Melihat matahari terbit dari gunung berapi itu tak terlupakan.

vocabulary.definition: something that happened to you; knowledge from doing a job

examples.en: She has a lot of experience in hotels.
examples.id: Dia punya banyak pengalaman di bidang perhotelan.

vocabulary.definition: in or to another country

examples.en: Have you ever travelled abroad?
examples.id: Apakah kamu pernah bepergian ke luar negeri?

vocabulary.definition: a person you work with

examples.en: I have lunch with my colleagues every day.
examples.id: Saya makan siang dengan rekan kerja setiap hari.

vocabulary.definition: the money you get every month for your job

examples.en: The salary is good, but the hours are long.
examples.id: Gajinya bagus, tetapi jam kerjanya panjang.

vocabulary.definition: working only some hours or days of the week

examples.en: He works part-time in a bookshop.
examples.id: Dia bekerja paruh waktu di toko buku.

vocabulary.definition: a period of time when a group of people work

examples.en: Nurses often work the night shift.
examples.id: Perawat sering bekerja sif malam.

vocabulary.definition: a person who buys things or services

examples.en: The shop had a lot of customers on Saturday.
examples.id: Toko itu punya banyak pelanggan hari Sabtu.

vocabulary.definition: to ask formally for a job, usually in writing

examples.en: I'd like to apply for the receptionist job.
examples.id: Saya ingin melamar pekerjaan resepsionis.

vocabulary.definition: a move to a better and more important job in the same company

examples.en: She hopes to get a promotion this year.
examples.id: Dia berharap mendapat kenaikan jabatan tahun ini.

vocabulary.definition: to take something from someone and give it back later

examples.en: Could I borrow your charger?
examples.id: Boleh saya pinjam pengisi dayamu?

vocabulary.definition: to give something to someone for a short time (past: lent)

examples.en: Could you lend me your umbrella?
examples.id: Bisakah kamu meminjamkan payungmu?

vocabulary.definition: a short piece of information that you send or leave for someone

examples.en: She isn't here. Can I take a message?
examples.id: Dia tidak ada. Mau titip pesan?

vocabulary.definition: to answer a message, letter or email

examples.en: Sorry I didn't reply to your email sooner.
examples.id: Maaf saya tidak membalas emailmu lebih cepat.

vocabulary.definition: to say that you will certainly do something

examples.en: I promise I'll call you tonight.
examples.id: Saya janji akan meneleponmu nanti malam.

vocabulary.definition: to try to find something or someone

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
examples.id: Saya sedang mencari kunci saya. Kamu melihatnya?

vocabulary.definition: to stop a machine, light or TV from working

examples.en: Please turn off your phones during the film.
examples.id: Mohon matikan ponsel selama film berlangsung.

examQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The concert tickets ___ very expensive, so we didn't buy them.
examQuestions.explanation: The concert tickets (jamak) di masa lalu → were.

examQuestions.prompt: Complete with the past simple of the verbs in brackets.
examQuestions.text: Last summer we ___ (fly) to Lombok and ___ (stay) in a small hotel near the beach.
examQuestions.explanation: fly → flew (tidak beraturan); stay → stayed (vokal + y → -ed).

examQuestions.text: A: ___ you watch the badminton final last night? B: No, I ___. I was at work.
examQuestions.explanation: Watch adalah kata kerja biasa di masa lalu → Did you watch...? No, I didn't.

examQuestions.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
examQuestions.explanation: Ketinggalan bus (sebab) → naik taksi (akibat). Sebab, so akibat.

examQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct option: My new laptop is ___ than my old one, and it's much lighter.
Rewrite the sentence so that it has the same meaning.
examQuestions.sentence: My brother is taller than me.
answers: I'm not as tall as my brother.
I am not as tall as my brother.
examQuestions.explanation: Kakak lebih tinggi = saya tidak setinggi kakak: not as tall as.

dialogue.speaker: Grandma
dialogue.text: I can't open this jar. It's too tight.

options: Give it to me. I'll open it for you.
I'm going to open it next week.
I opened it for you yesterday.
I'm opening it tomorrow at nine.

examQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct option: What ___ this evening? — I'm meeting some friends at the night market.
examQuestions.explanation: Menanyakan rencana yang sudah diatur → present continuous: What are you doing this evening?

examQuestions.prompt: Which sentences mean that something is NOT allowed? Choose all correct answers.
options: You don't have to buy a ticket.
Smoking is not allowed in the building.
examQuestions.explanation: Mustn't dan not allowed = dilarang. Don't have to = tidak perlu; shouldn't = saran.

examQuestions.prompt: Complete with the correct form of have to.
examQuestions.text: My sister is a pilot, so she ___ wear a uniform at work. I'm a writer, so I ___ wear one.
examQuestions.explanation: She → has to. Penulis tidak perlu memakai seragam → don't have to.

examQuestions.text: I ___ dinner when the electricity suddenly ___ off.
examQuestions.explanation: Kegiatan panjang → was cooking. Kejadian singkat yang menyela → went off.

examQuestions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
examQuestions.explanation: Have + you + ever + been to + tempat/acara.

examQuestions.sentence: She has never ate Indonesian food.
answers: She has never eaten Indonesian food.
examQuestions.explanation: Setelah has, pakai past participle: eaten.

examQuestions.prompt: Choose the correct option: Where's Tono? — He's ___ to the post office. He'll be back in ten minutes.

examQuestions.source: Dia berbicara bahasa Inggris dengan sangat baik.
examQuestions.explanation: Dengan sangat baik (menjelaskan kata kerja) = very well. Adverb diletakkan setelah objek.

examQuestions.prompt: Complete with much, many, a few or a little.
examQuestions.text: How ___ money do you need? — Just ___. About ten thousand rupiah for the bus.
examQuestions.explanation: Money tak terhitung → How much...? Sedikit (tak terhitung) → a little.

examQuestions.prompt: Choose the best word: Could you ___ me your pen, please? I left mine at home.
examQuestions.explanation: Meminta orang lain meminjamkan → lend. Borrow = meminjam (dari orang lain).

examQuestions.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with the best object.
examQuestions.explanation: put on your raincoat (memakai), fill in a form (mengisi), look for a job (mencari), pick up the children (menjemput).

placementQuestions.prompt: My sister ___ to the cinema with her friends last night.
I ___ like the film. It was really boring.
placementQuestions.explanation: Negatif past simple dengan kata kerja like → didn't like.

placementQuestions.prompt: Their house is ___ than ours. It has five bedrooms.
placementQuestions.explanation: Membandingkan dua rumah → comparative: bigger than.

placementQuestions.prompt: Look at those black clouds. It ___ rain.
placementQuestions.explanation: Prediksi dengan bukti → is going to.

placementQuestions.prompt: You look ill. You ___ see a doctor.
Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
placementQuestions.text: While I ___ (walk) to the station, I met an old friend.
placementQuestions.explanation: While + kegiatan panjang → past continuous: was walking.
Pengalaman (pernah pergi dan kembali) → Have you ever been to...?

placementQuestions.text: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge, but there are ___ eggs.
placementQuestions.explanation: Milk tak terhitung → much. Eggs terhitung → a few.

placementQuestions.prompt: Find the mistake in the sentence.
placementQuestions.explanation: Want diikuti to + base verb: want to learn.

placementQuestions.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a polite request.
acceptedAnswers: Could you please close the door?
placementQuestions.explanation: Could you + base verb + objek + please?

placementQuestions.prompt: Choose the best word: The hotel was very ___. It cost two million rupiah a night!
placementQuestions.explanation: Dua juta rupiah per malam → expensive (mahal).
